snp4.12:2.3: Which of these statements is true
snp4.12:2.4: when all of them say they are skilled?”
snp4.12:3.1:
“If, in not accepting
an opponent’s doctrine,
snp4.12:3.2: one’s a fool, a beast of inferior discernment,
snp4.12:3.3: then all are fools of inferior discernment—
snp4.12:3.4:
all of these
who dwell on their views.
snp4.12:4.1:
But if, in siding with a view,
one’s cleansed,
snp4.12:4.2:
with discernment made pure,
sensible, skilled,
snp4.12:4.3:
then none of them
are of inferior discernment,
snp4.12:4.4:
for all of them
have their own views.
snp4.12:5.1: I don’t say, ‘That’s how it is,’
snp4.12:5.2: the way fools tell one another.
snp4.12:5.3: They each make out their views to be true
snp4.12:5.4: and so regard their opponents as fools.”
snp4.12:6.1:
“What some say is true
—’That’s how it is’—
snp4.12:6.4:
Why can’t contemplatives
say one thing & the same?”
snp4.12:7.1:
“The truth is one,
there is no second
snp4.12:7.2:
about which a person who knows it
would argue with one who knows.
snp4.12:7.3:
Contemplatives promote
their various own truths,
snp4.12:7.4:
that’s why they don’t say
one thing & the same.”
snp4.12:8.1:
“But why do they say
various truths,
snp4.12:8.2: those who say they are skilled?
snp4.12:8.3: Have they learned many various truths
snp4.12:9.1:
“Apart from their perception
there are no
many
various
constant truths
in the world.
snp4.12:9.3:
Theorizing conjectures
with regard to views,
snp4.12:9.4:
they speak of a pair: true
& false.
snp4.12:10.1:
Dependent on what’s seen,
heard,
& sensed,
dependent on habits & practices,
snp4.12:10.3:
Taking a stance on his decisions,
praising himself,
snp4.12:10.4:
he says,
‘My opponent’s a fool & unskilled.’
snp4.12:11.1:
That by which
he regards his opponents as fools
snp4.12:11.2:
is that by which
he says he is skilled.
snp4.12:11.4:
he despises another
who speaks the same way.
snp4.12:12.1: Agreeing on a view gone out of bounds,
snp4.12:12.2: drunk with conceit, imagining himself perfect,
snp4.12:12.3:
he has consecrated, with his own mind,
himself
snp4.12:13.1:
If, by an opponent’s word,
one’s inferior,
snp4.12:13.2:
the opponent’s
of inferior discernment as well.
snp4.12:13.3:
But if, by one’s own word
one’s an attainer-of-knowledge, enlightened,
snp4.12:13.4:
no one
among contemplatives
is a fool.
snp4.12:14.1: ‘Those who approve of a doctrine other than this
snp4.12:14.3: That’s what the many sectarians say,
snp4.12:14.4:
for they’re smitten with passion
for their own views.
snp4.12:15.1:
‘Only here is there purity,’
that’s what they say.
snp4.12:15.2:
‘In no other doctrine
is purity,’ they say.
snp4.12:15.3:
That’s how the many sectarians
are entrenched,
snp4.12:15.4:
speaking firmly there
concerning their own path.
snp4.12:16.1: Speaking firmly concerning your own path,
snp4.12:16.2: what opponent here would you take as a fool?
snp4.12:16.3: You’d simply bring strife on yourself
snp4.12:16.4:
if you said your opponent’s a fool
with an impure doctrine.
snp4.12:17.1:
Taking a stance on your decisions,
& yourself as your measure,
snp4.12:17.2:
you dispute further down
into the world.
snp4.12:17.3:
But a person who’s abandoned
all decisions
snp4.12:17.4:
creates no strife
in the world.”
